newsitem.title: GERMANY: Former German fin min Apel open to delaying EMU.
newsitem.headline: Former German fin min Apel open to delaying EMU.

text.p: Former German Finance Minister Hans Apel said on Thursday a delay in Europe's monetary union (EMU) would be preferrable to launching a weak euro.
Apel, who served under former Chancellor Helmut Schmidt from 1974 to 1976 before becoming his defence minister, told German Radio that Bonn did not have to make a choice now.
"But one thing is absolutely clear," said Apel, still a member of the opposition Social Democratic Party (SPD) and now an economics professor.

"If, as it looks today, we will get a euro including almost all European currencies because we're all 'sinners' -- including the Germans -- then I can only say a delay is better than intro an euro that has no credibility.
"The world won't fall apart" if the euro is delayed, he said.

Gerhard Schroeder, the SPD Lower Saxony state premier who might be the party's challenger to Chancellor Helmut Kohl in the September 1998 election, said on Wednesday he preferred a delay in Europe's monetary union (EMU) if member countries cannot meet the Maastricht criteria.
But SPD chairman Oskar Lafontaine backs the scheduled 1999 starting date and Hesse state premier Hans Eichel, also SPD, said on Thursday that Schroeder was isolated in the party.
